newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu refuses to hold Zaire peace talks at sea.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu refuses to hold Zaire peace talks at sea.

text.p: Doubts grew over a planned meeting between embattled Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel chief Laurent Kabila after a U.S. source said Mobutu had turned down a proposal to hold the talks at sea.

The source, travelling with U.S. special envoy Bill Richardson, told Reuters that Mobutu had told Richardson on Tuesday he would not attend the talks on board a ship offered by South African President Nelson Mandela.

"Mobutu told Richardson there is no way he would be travelling to a ship for talks with Kabila. So once again the venue for the face-to-face meeting remains a problem," the source said after the U.S. envoy ended talks with Kabila late on Tuesday.
Any meeting would be the first between the two arch-rivals. Kabila's forces have captured half of the vast central African country since October and are advancing on the capital Kinshasa.
Kabila says talks must be brief and only discuss Mobutu's resignation, otherwise the rebel army will remove him by force.
"It will be a short ceremony on the issue of handing over power, otherwise we march on to Kinshasa," Kabila said.

Richardson, who met Mobutu in Kinshasa before flying to rebel-held Lubumbashi for talks with Kabila, referred to the latter as "president" -- apparently to drive home the U.S. position that Mobutu should step down.
The U.S. envoy will meet Mobutu for a second time on Wednesday after visiting Rwandan Hutu refugees in the rebel-held northeastern provincial capital Kisangani, Zaire's third city.
He might also visit Angola, accused by Kinshasa of invading Zaire to back the ethnic Tutsi-dominated rebels.

Richardson met Kabila late on Tuesday and his aide said the envoy raised concerns about the humanitarian crisis involving Rwandan Hutu refugees. Kabila promised aid agencies free access to the refugees, the aide said.

The rebel leader has issued a deadline to aid agencies, giving them 60 days to repatriate the Rwandan Hutus. The agencies said on Tuesday they had increasingly shocking reports of killings of Hutu refugees both around Kisangani and elsewhere.
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide in Rwanda that year.

Kabila told Reuters shortly before his talks with Richardson that pluralist elections could only be held after Mobutu stepped down or was overthrown, and even then the president and "his corrupt entourage cannot take part in such a process".

"There will be no compromise over the departure, through the battlefield or at talks, of Mobutu, his system and his henchmen," he said. "Mobutu and everything he represents must go before we can think of holding elections."

Kabila said his rebels were advancing by road on Kinshasa after capturing Kikwit town, 400 km (250 miles) from the capital. "We have advanced beyond Kikwit. Our destination is Kinshasa," he said, adding his forces had also taken Kikwit airport.
A regional military source who closely monitors the war said rebels planned to move troops and equipment through the airport for the final assault on Kinshasa.
Richardson said he had "very fruitful" talks with Mobutu earlier on Tuesday in Kinshasa and suggested a good time for the first meeting between the two enemies would be this weekend.
"I have agreed to (South African) President (Nelson) Mandela's request that I meet Mr Mobutu on a ship off the Atlantic coastline to discuss Mr Mobutu's departure," Kabila said.
"As far as I am concerned this will be a short ceremony at which Mr Mobutu is supposed to agree to leave, otherwise our forces now advancing on the route to Kinshasa will eject him."
South Africa said on Tuesday it hoped to host the talks between Mobutu and Kabila before the weekend -- on a former Russian naval ship dubbed the "Grey Diplomat".
Mobutu, who has cancer, has ruled out South Africa as a venue as too far on health grounds. Kabila ruled out Congo's capital Brazzaville, over the river from Kinshasa, and Gabon on security grounds.
